_meta.title: Family and Friends 5 — Curriculum Map
_meta.note: Covers Grade 4→5 transition. All 8 units + 4 review sections catalogued.

units.title: That's a big family!
vocabularySets: Extended family members (aunt, uncle, cousin, nephew, niece, grandparents)
Physical appearance (curly, straight, wavy, bald, tall, slim, elderly)
units.phonics: oy sound (boy, toy, enjoy, annoy, destroy)
units.readingSkill: Reading a family tree and profile descriptions
units.writingSkill: Writing a description of a family member
units.speakingTask: Describe a relative to a partner without naming them
units.listeningTask: Identify family members from audio descriptions
units.project: Make a class family tree poster
keyLearningObjectives: Name at least 8 extended family members
Use adjectives to describe physical appearance
Form present perfect sentences with 'just'
Read and understand a family profile

units.title: Amazing animals!
vocabularySets: Animal classification (endangered, extinct, predator, prey, mammal, reptile, amphibian, insect)
Habitats (ocean, rainforest, desert, Arctic, Antarctic, grassland, mountain)
units.phonics: air sound (chair, hair, fair, there, wear, care, share)
units.values: Caring for the environment and wildlife
units.speakingTask: Ask and answer 'Have you ever...?' questions about animals
units.listeningTask: Listen to animal descriptions and match to habitats
units.project: Create an endangered animal awareness poster
units.cultureLink: Wildlife conservation projects in the UK and Australia
keyLearningObjectives: Classify animals by type and habitat
Describe what makes an animal endangered
Form and respond to 'Have you ever...?' questions
Write a structured fact file

units.title: Hard work!
vocabularySets: Chore verbs (vacuum, mop, dust, sweep, polish, iron, rake, weed, tidy)
Frequency adverbs (always, usually, often, sometimes, rarely, never)
units.grammar: have to / don't have to (obligation and lack of obligation)
units.phonics: ear sound (ear, hear, near, fear, clear, weird, here)
units.values: Taking responsibility and helping at home
units.readingSkill: Reading a survey about household chores
units.writingSkill: Writing about your daily chores routine
units.listeningTask: Listen and complete a chore schedule
keyLearningObjectives: Name and describe at least 8 household chores
Use frequency adverbs correctly in sentences
Express obligation and lack of obligation with have to/don't have to
Read and extract information from a survey

units.title: Feeling good!
vocabularySets: Ailments (headache, stomachache, backache, earache, toothache, sore throat, cold, fever, rash, sprain)
Health actions (rest, drink fluids, take medicine, see a doctor, apply ice, stay in bed)
units.phonics: ure sound (sure, cure, pure, future, picture, nature, creature)
units.values: Taking care of your health and helping others
units.writingSkill: Writing an advice letter to a friend who is ill
units.listeningTask: Listen to health complaints and match to advice
keyLearningObjectives: Name at least 8 common illnesses and ailments
Give appropriate health advice using should/shouldn't
Role-play a doctor–patient interaction
Write a structured advice letter

units.title: Let's have lunch
vocabularySets: Food containers (jar, can/tin, bag, box, bottle, carton, packet, tube, bunch, loaf)
Food adjectives (fresh, organic, frozen, tinned, dried, raw, cooked, spicy, mild, sweet, sour)
units.grammar: Countable and uncountable nouns; some/any; how much/how many
units.phonics: Long oo (food, moon, school, blue) vs short oo (book, foot, cook, good)
units.values: Healthy eating and reducing food waste
units.writingSkill: Writing a shopping list and simple recipe
units.speakingTask: Plan a meal using a budget — discuss what to buy
units.listeningTask: Listen to a shopping conversation and note items
units.project: Create a class recipe book page
units.cultureLink: Food traditions in the UK, USA, and Australia
keyLearningObjectives: Name food containers and the foods they hold
Distinguish countable and uncountable nouns
Use some/any and how much/how many correctly
Read and write a simple recipe

units.title: Be safe!
vocabularySets: Safety equipment (helmet, seatbelt, life jacket, safety goggles, knee pads, reflective vest, first aid kit)
Hazard words (dangerous, risky, slippery, fragile, poisonous, flammable, sharp, unstable, toxic)
units.phonics: ow (now, town, brown, crowd) vs ow (show, know, grow, blow)
units.values: Personal safety and looking out for others
units.writingSkill: Writing safety rules for a place (playground, kitchen, road)
units.speakingTask: Discuss safety rules for different activities
units.listeningTask: Listen to safety announcements and note the rules
units.project: Design a safety poster for school
units.cultureLink: Road safety rules in different countries
keyLearningObjectives: Name safety equipment and explain when to use it
Identify and describe hazards
Use must/mustn't to express rules and prohibition
Write a clear set of safety rules

units.title: Technology
units.topic: Modern technology and predictions about the future
vocabularySets: Technology items (robot, tablet, laptop, smartphone, solar panel, electric car, drone, 3D printer, virtual reality headset)
Technology verbs (download, upload, charge, connect, install, recharge, stream, search, programme, control)
units.phonics: tion suffix (action, station, invention, information, education, pollution, solution)
units.writingSkill: Writing predictions about technology in 50 years
units.speakingTask: Debate: Is technology good or bad for children?
units.listeningTask: Listen to a technology news report
units.project: Draw and describe your invention of the future
units.cultureLink: Tech companies and inventions from English-speaking countries
keyLearningObjectives: Name and describe at least 8 technology items
Use technology action verbs correctly
Make predictions using will/won't
Write a paragraph of future predictions

units.title: Art and music
units.topic: Art forms, musical instruments, and creative expression
vocabularySets: Art forms (sculpture, photography, pottery, street art, watercolour, portrait, landscape, abstract, collage)
Musical instruments (violin, trumpet, drums, guitar, flute, piano, saxophone, harp, cello, clarinet)
units.grammar: Defining relative clauses with who / which / that
units.phonics: Silent letters: k (knife, know, knight, kneel); b (climb, comb, thumb, lamb)
units.values: Appreciating art and music in all its forms
units.readingSkill: Reading an artist or musician biography
units.speakingTask: Present a famous artist or musician to the class
units.listeningTask: Listen to music samples and identify instruments
units.project: Create an art exhibition with descriptions
units.cultureLink: Famous artists and musicians from English-speaking countries
keyLearningObjectives: Name and describe at least 6 art forms and 8 instruments
Use defining relative clauses with who/which/that
Read and understand a biography
Write a structured biography

fluencyTimeSections.scenario: Meeting someone new at a family reunion
Visiting a doctor / giving health advice
Shopping at a supermarket or market
